data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The answer is 18, verified by the property that 18-3=15 is divisible by 5 and 18-4=14 is divisible by 7, confirming both congruences, and 18 is minimal because the only positive integers below 18 in the x\u22613 mod 5 class are {3, 8, 13}, none of which satisfy x\u22614 mod 7.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If an integer below 18 outside the x\u22613 mod 5 class could satisfy x\u22613 mod 5, the exhaustiveness argument fails\u2014 but this is impossible by definition of the residue class.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 18 does not satisfy both congruences, the answer is wrong.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If there are more candidates below 18 in the residue class than {3,8,13}, the enumeration is incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Exhaustive verification: The set of positive integers satisfying x\u22613 mod 5 and x<18 is {3, 8, 13}. Check each: 3 mod 7=3\u22604, 8 mod 7=1\u22604, 13 mod 7=6\u22604. None satisfy the second congruence. Since 18 satisfies both (18 mod 5=3, 18 mod 7=4) and all smaller candidates in the first residue class fail, 18 is the smallest positive solution. The gap between consecutive candidates in the x\u22613 mod 5 class is 5, and we checked all three below 18, covering the entire range [1,17].","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
